Fractional — a small group pools funds for a bigger parcel, sharing cost and risk, at the price of needing agreement among partners. Whichever model: the land’s own title must be registered in identifiable names, not lost inside a scheme. What to check before you commit Papers and position outrank projections. Water : a cheap plot with no reliable source is not a bargain, it is a liability — borewells genuinely run dry in rocky belts, and waterless land carries a different risk profile at any price. Then the full drill : title deed and chain, EC, survey boundaries, land classification, zoning status. Access : legal road access, not a neighbour’s goodwill. Definition — Water security: year-round availability from borewell, canal or tank — checked in summer, not monsoon. It is the single physical factor that most separates farmland that holds value from farmland that stalls. Red flags Ownership disputes and murky chains; wrong survey boundaries; missing ECs; classification problems; water scarcity; zoning restrictions the seller forgot to mention; and — the soft one — return projections that only work if everything goes right. Any one of these changes the price; several together change the decision. How farmland compares with other assets Asset Typical return profile Liquidity Best suited for Managed farmland Varies — appreciation + uncertain crop income Low Long-term diversification, not quick gains Urban apartment ~6–9% (rent + appreciation) Medium Income plus moderate growth Gold ETF ~6–8% High Liquid store of value Index fund ~10–14%, volatile High (daily) Long-term growth, risk-tolerant money Farmland does not compete on liquidity or explosive upside. It competes on stability, inflation resistance, and being a real thing you can stand on, gift, and pass down. Is it reliable? The structure is sound — patient holders in genuine corridors have done very well. Failures follow one pattern: an unchecked title, an unreliable water source, or crop income that never arrived. None of these are hidden risks; all are checkable before the advance. Checking them is standard practice, not paranoia. Pre-purchase checklist ☐ Eligibility under the state’s purchase rules. ☐ Title deed + ownership history verified. ☐ Fresh EC. ☐ Survey boundaries and extent confirmed on the ground. ☐ Classification and zoning verified. ☐ Year-round water availability checked. ☐ Road connectivity and access assessed. ☐ Holding model chosen deliberately (freehold / fractional / managed). ☐ Crop projections discounted; appreciation case evaluated on its own. Quick answers (FAQ) Is farmland near a city a good investment now? In real corridors, at farmland-honest prices, on an appreciation thesis — yes, as patient money. Is agricultural income really tax-free? Genuine agricultural income is exempt — but that is a reason operators DRESS returns as farm income, not a reason to believe the projection. Managed vs unmanaged? Managed buys convenience and adds operator risk; unmanaged buys control and adds workload. Bottom line Buy the corridor, not the crop chart. Water, title and zoning decide the decade; the brochure decides nothing.
